sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.8% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, reaching $31.7 billion [F1][F9][F198].
Operating income grew faster, a 5.8% CAGR to $8.6 billion, lifting operating margin from 22.9% to 27.2% [F10][F19][F199][F20][F28].
FY2022 was the step change in the top line, revenue up 17.1%, as rate cases, favorable weather and volumes lifted results [D239][P26].
FY2020 was the trough, net income down 63.3% on impairment charges and COVID-19 volume losses [D157][P60].
Electric Utilities and Infrastructure supplied 90.9% of FY2025 revenue and 3.6pp of its 5.6% growth [D541][D543][D358].
Residential electric was the largest single driver, 43.3% of revenue and 2.8pp of FY2025 growth [D774][D776].
Gas Utilities and Infrastructure added 2.0pp, with Piedmont Natural Gas up 32.1% and contributing 1.7pp [D566][D682][D683].
FY2024's 59.2% net income growth came from rate increases and riders, improved weather and higher volumes [D320][P18].
Operating income grew 8.8% against 5.6% revenue growth in FY2025, an incremental margin of 41.4% [D359][D358][D378].
FY2025 operating margin of 27.2% is the window high, 4.3pp above the 22.9% median and 7.5pp above the FY2020 low [F28][D932][D933][D931].
Operating expenses grew 5.3% against 5.6% revenue growth, so the margin added only 0.8pp [D372][D358][D370].
D&A rose to 24.3% of revenue in FY2025 from 21.4% in FY2024, the main cost drag [D341][D303].
Net margin of 15.7% sits below the 16.0% window high and the 17.6% peer median [F47][D935][D952].
The FY2025 effective tax rate of 11.2% kept net margin close to operating margin [D345][F47][F28].
Operating cash flow of $12.3 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025, in line with the 2.19x to 3.48x range since FY2019 [F77][F38][D346][D97][D268].
Capex of $14.0 billion, 44.2% of revenue and 1.82x D&A, pushed free cash flow to -$1.7 billion [F87][D342][D348][F97].
Free cash flow margin of -5.3% is better than the -5.8% window median but far from the 0.2% FY2024 high [D343][D939][D938].
FY2022's -$5.4 billion free cash flow reflected fuel undercollections that increased borrowings until recovery [F94][P36].
Net debt reached $89.6 billion in FY2025, 282.3% of revenue, from $50.0 billion in FY2016 [D352][D353][D14].
That net cash position ranks in the 25th percentile of four utilities peers, whose median is -228.4% of revenue [D953][D954].
The current ratio fell to 0.55x, below the 0.66x window median, as current liabilities rose 8.7% [F177][D945][D369].
Diluted shares rose 0.6% to 777 million in FY2025, so EPS growth of 10.5% outpaced net income growth of 9.8% [X115][D374][D361][D360].
The current ratio of 0.55x is below 1.0x and near the 0.53x window low, leaving little short-term cushion [F177][D943][R1].
Cash of $245 million covers only 0.1 years of the latest burn [F137][D356][R2].
Net cash has fallen for nine straight years, from -$50.0 billion in FY2016 to -$89.6 billion in FY2025 [D14][D352][R3].
Free cash flow has run below 80% of net income for three years, at -0.96x, 0.01x and -0.34x [D269][D309][D347][R4].
If FY2026 operating margin falls below the 22.9% window median, the margin expansion trend has reversed [D933].
Free cash flow margin recovering above the -5.8% window median would signal capex is being absorbed [D939].
A current ratio below the 0.53x window low would confirm the liquidity squeeze [D943].
